reason: Conversation 2 gets the homeowner to the answer: it explains the switched spur, tells her to look for a switch labelled for the washer, and the customer finds it OFF and turns it on, which fixes the machine. It also gives a clear safe-use instruction and a useful tip to label the switch. Its one flaw is suggesting easing the machine forward if the switch is on, which goes against the safety boundary for an integrated unit, but it was never needed here. Conversation 1 mentioned the spur early but never told her to look for or check the switch after explaining it, wandered into plug-fuse advice she had said she could not do, asked repetitive questions, and ended by escalating to an appliance engineer with a wrong diagnosis (power cord/plug), which would have wasted time and money for a no-fault situation.
